summary: Reflection on the latest Design trends from our team's recent trip to Bologna, Italy. Matte White, graphically softer tapware, large format tiles and more. By Tony Rowlands.
title: Design Watch: Bathroom Design Trends From Cersaie, Italy
bodyHtml:
Matte White, Softer Tapware Finishes, Graphically Restrained

After returning from Italy visiting our manufacturing partners, we can confirm that 2023 will be a big year indeed with cutting edge design and technology at the forefront.

Some of our new products will completely redefine their category and even establish new ones.

Certainly the team was interested in the design trends and we are seeing ascendance of matte white basins and Wc's backed by stainless steel tapware and accessories as a major design direction.

The look is trending softer and more restrained particularly without solid finishes on the tapware and with stainless creating a ghosting effect , much less overwhelming and softer graphically.

Tiles: Large Format, Bold

Of course tiles are the background to our products and there was a lot to see there.

It is totally a story of large format porcelain even when imitating smaller format tiles. Almost seamless installation and virtually no grout!

The marble finishes were extraordinary with a new emphasis on mimicking coloured stone. Blue; green, red, pink no longer just the standard Calacatta and Arabescato.

Also wonderful Limestones.

Wallpaper Pattern, Large Scale Design, Spectacular Colour

Another big trend was what we termed "wallpaper patterns "/ large scale designs in spectacular colourways.

In Australia more likely to be used in powder rooms.

Even the plain colours were dialled up just a little in intensity creating a moody effect.

We caught up with several of our distributors who sell tiles and they confirmed our assessment.

Glen Brooking from our distributor Colortile remarked on the extraordinary quality of the digital print images and that they are trending to the 1200 x 3200mm format for both residential and commercial projects.

Also present was John Cannella from Harvey Norman. John concluded that the fair had two clear standouts - bigger is better with an array of larger format marble look tiles, and that the industry has made significant improvements to design and manufacturing processes with amazing results .

John also noted that bright, bold and happy colours was another notable trend. Great for smaller tiles enhancing the look and mood in any space.

Thanks for reading!
